title: Comunicado 2025-01-30
summary: The SARB MPC cut the repo rate 25bp (to 7.50%) on a split 4-2 vote, with two members preferring to hold, framing the move as reducing the degree of restrictiveness to make the stance 'somewhat more neutral'. The cut rests on benign near-term inflation (3% in December, expectations aligned with the 4.5% midpoint, core at or below the midpoint) and an output gap expected to close, but the committee assessed inflation risks to the upside and all members worried about the global outlook: a strong dollar, limited Fed space, possible US hikes, tariffs and administered prices. Guidance is deliberately non-committal ('no forward guidance and no pre-commitment'), with the QPM path drifting only slightly lower to around 7.25%, and a trade-war scenario showing rates 50bp higher at peak. This is the first statement in the base, so there is no previous statement to compare against; on its own it reads as a cautious cut with a divided committee and limited further easing in view.

key_quotes.quote: Four members preferred this action, while two supported an unchanged stance.
key_quotes.context: Split 4-2 vote on the 25bp cut, two members for a hold

key_quotes.quote: The committee ultimately agreed that it was possible to reduce the degree of policy restrictiveness, making the stance somewhat more neutral.
key_quotes.context: Rationale for the cut: stance still restrictive, moving toward neutral

key_quotes.quote: with no forward guidance and no pre-commitment to any specific rate path
key_quotes.context: No easing guidance; QPM path only drifts slightly lower to ~7.25%

key_quotes.quote: The risks to the inflation outlook are assessed to the upside.
key_quotes.context: Upside inflation risks from the external environment and administered prices despite benign near-term inflation
